title: Question 4

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
When the device is at position $P$, a stationary wave is formed between the device and the sheet.

Explain how the stationary wave, including the nodes and the antinodes, is formed.

markscheme_points.text: The incident and reflected waves superpose
(resultant) amplitude is maximum at an antinode
(resultant) amplitude is minimum/zero at a node

hints: Hint 1: Think about what happens when the outgoing microwave hits the large metal sheet - can it pass through or must it come back?
Hint 2: You now have two waves travelling in opposite directions along the same line XY with the same frequency and wavelength - what principle describes what happens when they meet?
Hint 3: At some points the two waves always arrive in phase and reinforce - what name is given to a point of maximum resultant amplitude?
Hint 4: At other points the two waves always arrive in antiphase and cancel - what name is given to a point of minimum or zero resultant amplitude?
parts.proper_answer: The microwave from the emitter reflects at the metal sheet. The incident and reflected waves travelling in opposite directions superpose. Where they superpose constructively the resultant amplitude is maximum, forming an antinode. Where they superpose destructively the resultant amplitude is minimum or zero, forming a node.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Reflection to give two opposite waves**
You have an emitter sending microwaves toward the metal sheet along XY. Metal reflects microwaves, so a reflected wave travels back from the sheet toward the device. You now have incident and reflected waves of the same frequency, wavelength and speed travelling in opposite directions in the same region.

Step 2: **Superposition creates a stationary pattern**
When two coherent waves occupy the same space their displacements add by the principle of superposition. Because they travel oppositely, the interference pattern does not move along - it is a stationary wave with fixed positions of large and small vibration.

Step 3: **Antinodes and nodes explained**
At an antinode the incident and reflected waves are always in phase, so constructive interference gives maximum resultant amplitude. At a node they are always in antiphase, so destructive interference gives minimum or zero resultant amplitude.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the wavelength of the microwaves.
hints: Hint 1: Microwaves are electromagnetic waves in a vacuum, so what speed do they travel at and what link connects speed, frequency and wavelength?
Hint 2: Check the frequency unit - 6.3 GHz means $6.3 \times 10^9$ Hz - then rearrange for wavelength before substituting.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Choose the wave equation**
For all electromagnetic waves in vacuum, speed $c = 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. The governing relation is: $$c = f \lambda$$

Step 2: **Substitute and calculate**
Rearrange for wavelength: $$\lambda = c / f$$ $$\lambda = \frac{3.0 \times 10^8}{6.3 \times 10^9} = 0.0476\text{ m}$$ To 2 significant figures, $\lambda = 0.048\text{ m}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
At point $P$ the receiver detects a maximum amplitude of the stationary wave.

The device is moved slowly from point $P$ along the line $XY$ and the receiver detects a series of minimum and maximum amplitudes. The first time a minimum amplitude is detected by the receiver is when the device is at point $Q$.

Determine the distance between $P$ and $Q$.
hints: Hint 1: P is a maximum (antinode) and Q is the very next minimum (node) - recall what fraction of a wavelength separates an adjacent node and antinode.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Adjacent maximum to minimum is a quarter wavelength**
In a stationary wave, successive nodes are $\lambda/2$ apart and successive antinodes are $\lambda/2$ apart. So a node is $\lambda/4$ from the next antinode. Here P is an antinode and Q is the first node, so: $$PQ = \frac{\lambda}{4} = \frac{0.048}{4} = 0.012\text{ m}$$

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The intensity of the microwaves emitted by the device is increased. The frequency of the microwaves is unchanged. The device is moved slowly along the line $XY$ from point $Q$ until the next maximum amplitude is detected at point $R$.

State and explain whether the distance $QR$ is greater than, less than or the same as distance $PQ$.

markscheme_points.text:
(Distance QR is the) same (as PQ) and one of:
• Distance (between maxima / minima) does not depend on intensity
• distance depends only on wavelength
• wavelength is unchanged / constant

hints: Hint 1: Increasing intensity makes the wave louder or brighter but does it change the frequency or wavelength set by the emitter?
parts.proper_answer: Distance QR is the same as PQ. Frequency and hence wavelength are unchanged, and node spacing depends only on wavelength, not on intensity.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **What controls the spacing?**
The distance from a minimum at Q to the next maximum at R is again $\lambda/4$. Spacing depends only on $\lambda$, and $\lambda = c/f$ with $f$ unchanged. Increasing intensity increases amplitude only, not $f$ or $\lambda$. So QR is the same as PQ.
